excerpts:
No matter when you knew, you knew it was coming. A game for the ages from Amon-Ra St. Brown, one of Germany's finest, back in a place of familiarity.

"It was a memorable three days, three days that I'll never forget," St. Brown said after the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. "My first game in Germany, a place that I call basically my second home."

Everything this week was about St. Brown.

The Lions recorded a season-high 495 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs offered a casual 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns on 29 touches. Goff, on an off day, threw for 303 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. The Lions converted 53.3 percent of their third-down tries, averaged 7.2 yards per play and rushed for 191 yards.

suffered an ankle injury on the first series and did not return to Sunday's [35-10 loss](https://www.nfl.com/games/patriots-at-lions-2026-reg-10) to the Detroit Lions in Munich.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update after the game on the severity of Maye's injury, which he called a lower leg injury, adding that the QB will "get more tests run."

"He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level," Vrabel said, explaining the decision to rule out Maye.

Maye was initially deemed questionable to return before being downgraded in the second quarter.

The third-year QB was 3-of-4 passing for 48 yards, with an 11-yard scramble, at the time of his exit.
